topics.topic: Whether MigrationClosure identity is global by digest or scoped to a store history
questions: If separate store histories successfully accept files with the same digest, do their MigrationClosure records have the same entity identity or distinct identities scoped by store history?

If a pre-import backup is restored and the same file is successfully imported again, is the new closure the same entity because its sole identity is the same digest, or a distinct entity scoped to the new store history?

Is the digest a globally sufficient identity, making acceptance of the same file after a pre-import backup restore a continuation or recreation of the same entity, or is MigrationClosure identity scoped by the store or store history as well as the digest?

quotes:
It is identified by the digest of the file the import accepted, the one
identity it has (codex round-04 T1); Registry mints no identifier for it.

Durable, a record of its own, at most one per store (R0-89): an instance that
restores a store from before the import may import again, and that store
then holds its own closure.
judgement.why: Registry has no operation that compares closures across store histories, and pointers and audit entries name only the digest, so treating equal-digest closures as globally identical or store-scoped changes no observable product action.

topics.topic: Whether the accepted M10 decision made MigrationClosure a value or an entity
questions: Was the owner's 2026-10-31 acceptance of M10 an acceptance of the then-written value model, as the Status says, or a decision that it is an entity as this passage says?

How can this be reconciled with the Status statement that on 2026-10-31 “the proposals under M01, M04 and M10 are accepted as written,” when M10 was then declared a value: did the owner accept value identity, accept only the record-of-its-own facts, or decide entity identity?

Did the accepted 2026-10-31 M10 decision make MigrationClosure the value embedded in StoreHistory described by the accepted draft, or the independently persisted entity that the changed M10 attributes to that same decision?

quotes:
Until
2026-11-11 it was declared a value; the owner's decision of 2026-10-31 that
it is a record of its own, addressed by the pointers and the audit, is what
SPEC_STANDARD §15.1.1 calls an entity.
judgement.why: The current text explicitly says that the accepted record-of-its-own decision entails entity identity and that the former value declaration lasted only until its correction.

topics.topic: How a pre-existing nonempty store acquires its required AuditSequence
questions: How does a non-empty store that already exists when M12 is introduced acquire its required AuditSequence record, and what value and identity does that record receive?
How does a pre-existing nonempty store that already has audit history acquire its required exactly-one AuditSequence when this model is introduced?

quotes:
The last audit sequence number a store's history ever wrote (M09; State 2 A15
rule 5), kept apart from the entries so that erasing old entries never lowers
it and a number is never reused (R0-66). Exactly one per store. Added on
2026-11-11: States 2 and 3 kept it durable without a model that holds it.
judgement.why: M12 gives an already-durable audit counter a model home; its addition to State 1 is not a runtime event that introduces the value into previously conforming stores.

topics.topic: Whether an imported ArtifactPointer names MigrationClosure or the publishing actor as publisher
questions: Does an imported artifact pointer name the MigrationClosure record as its publisher, or does it name the owner or agent who published it as R0-88 requires?

Does an imported pointer name the MigrationClosure entity as its publisher, or must it name the acting owner as required by R0-88's statement that pointers record who published them and that only the agent through Kernel or the owner publishes?

quotes:
A pointer the import brings in (R0-50) was published before Registry recorded
principals: the v1 Registry keeps no publisher (its `owner_service` is the
caller's own claim, checked by no token) and no withdrawal (L22). Its
publisher is therefore the import itself — the migration closure (M10), not a
principal — and its published and superseded instants are those the source
holds ("Revisions and times"). It is never imported `withdrawn`, so it carries
no withdrawal facts until it is withdrawn in Registry, which records them as
for any pointer (owner, 2026-10-31; codex round-02 T1).
judgement.why: The text explicitly distinguishes an imported pointer from a pointer published in Registry and assigns the migration closure as the imported pointer's publisher.

topics.topic: Whether every State 1 model must have complete typed field declarations
questions: Replace the deferral of model field names and types with complete typed field declarations for every State 1 model; only answer shapes and other matters outside model structure may remain deferred.
Replace the deferral of model field names and types with complete typed field declarations for every State 1 model, including M10 MigrationClosure and M12 AuditSequence.

quotes:
Field names, types,
formal optionality and every answer shape belong to State 6; orders, replay
mechanisms, correction semantics and token scopes belong to State 2 (State 0,
"Carried to later states"; codex round-01 T5).
judgement.why: The blanket deferral of model field names and types violates the State 1 standard's requirement that every field be declared with its type.

topics.topic: Whether restore creates a new AuditSequence identity or continues the backed-up entity
questions: When a backup with an older sequence number replaces a later lost store, is the carried AuditSequence the same entity whose value has gone backward, or a new store-history entity initialized from the backup; and what action is considered to create that entity if Registry creates one only with a new empty store?

Since M12 is identified by the store that holds it while R0-89 says a restored store begins its own history from the backup, is the restored AuditSequence the same entity, or a new entity initialized with the backed-up number?

quotes:
Registry has no restore operation (R0-89): the owner puts a backup in the
place of a lost store, outside Registry, and Registry starts on it as on any
store. A restored store holds this record as the backup holds it, the same
record continued; Registry neither knows nor records that the store was
restored.

A store restored from a backup after a loss
  begins its own history from the backup's last number (R0-89);
judgement.why: The restored backup continues the same backed-up AuditSequence record, while the restored store's new history continues numbering from the value contained in that backup.

topics.topic: Whether AuditSequence or retained audit entries are authoritative for the last sequence number
questions: Is the independently persisted AuditSequence record authoritative for the last number, or must the current audit entries be treated as the source of truth even after old entries are erased?

quotes:
The last audit sequence number a store's history ever wrote (M09; State 2 A15
rule 5), kept apart from the entries so that erasing old entries never lowers
it and a number is never reused (R0-66). Exactly one per store. Added on
2026-11-11: States 2 and 3 kept it durable without a model that holds it.

Facts: the last sequence number, a whole number — 0 for a store made new,
then moved to each new entry's number in that entry's transaction, and by
nothing else; never lowered.

None. It is read only inside Registry: by the audit append, which takes the
next number, and by a backup, which records the number in its own readable
record (State 2 A18); no answer returns it.
judgement.why: The durable AuditSequence record, not the surviving entry set, supplies the number read by an append and is moved transactionally with each new entry.

topics.topic: Which product actions may read MigrationClosure
questions: Which product actions may read MigrationClosure: only the import guard and backup machinery, or also an owner-facing import-status read, pointer reads, audit reads, or another operation?

topics.topic: Who derives the MigrationClosure identity digest and from which authoritative file representation
questions: Who produces the digest that becomes the entity's identity, and from which authoritative representation of the accepted file: Registry from the received bytes, the external migration script, or the owner as import input?
